paper.title: SkillForge: Forging Domain-Specific, Self-Evolving Agent Skills in Cloud Technical Support
paper.central_claim: SkillForge closes a creation-evaluation-refinement loop for enterprise agent skills: a Domain-Contextualized Skill Creator mines tickets and knowledge bases to produce better initial skills than a generic creator, and a Failure Analyzer -> Skill Diagnostician -> Skill Optimizer pipeline traces execution failures to skill deficiencies and rewrites the skill, progressively improving quality from expert-authored, domain-created and generic starting points, to the point that automated evolution can surpass manually curated expert knowledge.
paper.claim_scope: Five cloud technical-support scenarios of one provider, 1,883 tickets / 3,737 single-turn tasks, Qwen3-Max, chronological 25/25/25/25 split (3 evolution rounds, last split held out), LLM-judged consistency rate vs historical expert replies.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref unavailable to the worker subagent at write time; model_type recorded per controller dispatch instruction (agent_model=haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

evidence.quote: existing skill creators lack domain grounding, producing skills poorly aligned with real-world task requirements.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap 1: generic skill creators lack domain grounding.

evidence.quote: there is no systematic mechanism to trace execution failures back to skill deficiencies and drive targeted refinements, leaving skill quality stagnant despite accumulating operational evidence.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap 2: no failure-to-skill-defect mechanism.

evidence.quote: results from the four dimensions are combined by deterministic rules into a single verdict
evidence.support_explanation: Failure Analyzer: four LLM dimensions (Knowledge, Tool, Clarification, Style) merged by deterministic code rules into a structured verdict.

evidence.quote: Skill Understanding
evidence.support_explanation: Diagnostician is a ReAct agent with four stages (Skill Understanding, Evidence Collection, Root Cause Attribution, Plan Generation) that outputs a machine-parsable optimization plan.

evidence.quote: Minimal Modification (only change what is necessary to address diagnosed issues), Do No Harm (preserve existing correct behaviors via additive changes; never delete working content), and Evidence-Based (every change traces to specific failure-analysis evidence).
evidence.support_explanation: Optimizer principles; they are instructions, not a tested regression gate.

evidence.quote: ensuring full traceability.
evidence.support_explanation: Each optimized state is committed as Skill_v_n+1 (versioning); no accept/reject step precedes the commit.

evidence.quote: tickets are sorted chronologically and partitioned into four equal-sized splits (25% each).
evidence.support_explanation: Chronological split design.

evidence.quote: never seen during evolution
evidence.support_explanation: The fourth split is the held-out evaluation set (continuation of the sentence: "the fourth split is held out as the evaluation set ... never seen during evolution").

evidence.quote: The first three splits form the development set and are fed sequentially to the three evolution rounds (v1, v2, v3) to simulate bad cases arriving in production batches over time
evidence.support_explanation: Evolution rounds consume successive dev splits.

evidence.quote: Bad cases are identified through automated LLM-judge filtering.
evidence.support_explanation: An LLM-judge both identifies bad cases for evolution and provides the evaluation metric; judge model not named (all experiments use Qwen3-Max, E21).

evidence.quote: for skill quality evaluation, comparing the agent’s response against expert reference responses from historical tickets.
evidence.support_explanation: Metric: LLM-judged Consistency Rate vs the single historical expert reply.

evidence.quote: We validated the LLM-judge against human annotations on a sample subset
evidence.support_explanation: Judge validation subset size and judge model are not stated (>90% agreement with human consensus).

evidence.quote: Each offline evaluation is repeated 3 times; we report the mean.
evidence.support_explanation: Three repeats, only the mean is reported; no standard deviations or intervals.
Held-out Strict (Lenient) CR deltas per round for S_manual, S_domain, S_generic; absolute values are not given.
Initial-skill quality; S_manual absolute scores are not reported, and the evaluation split used for this table is not stated.

evidence.quote: Skills generated by a generic skill creator (Claude Code with Claude-Sonnet-4.5) augmented with domain-specific tool schemas mined from historical tickets
evidence.support_explanation: S_generic comes from a different creator model and is denied domain knowledge/tickets by privacy constraints (Sec.3.1.3); confounded comparison.

evidence.quote: indicating that automated evolution can surpass human-curated knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Claim that evolution surpasses expert knowledge, inferred from the gain of S_manual itself.

evidence.quote: The skill-equipped agent achieves +13.76pp Strict CR over this legacy system on the same held-out set
evidence.support_explanation: Comparison to a production decision-tree + prompt system; which skill variant and absolute numbers are unspecified.

evidence.quote: Knowledge failures, however, plateau after v1 (0% further reduction in v2)
evidence.support_explanation: Reported limit: knowledge failures plateau.

evidence.quote: Together these factors point to an inherent ceiling for purely text-based, fully automated skill optimization
evidence.support_explanation: Authors admit a ceiling and a need for human review of the long tail.

evidence.quote: All experiments use the latest version of Qwen3-Max as the backbone LLM.
evidence.support_explanation: Single backbone (the model/version of the judge is not separately stated).

evidence.quote: optimize instructions via search or text-based gradients.
evidence.support_explanation: Prompt-level optimizers (APE, OPRO, TextGrad) are cited as related work, not run as baselines.

evidence.quote: SkillForge differs from these approaches in two key respects
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated differentiation: targets the skill artifact and uses a three-stage pipeline.

evidence.quote: self-generated skills provide no benefit
evidence.support_explanation: Cited SkillsBench finding that self-generated skills give no benefit (context for the creator and the evolution loop).

evidence.quote: In this paper we use offline replays of historical tickets
evidence.support_explanation: Offline replay; no online deployment loop is run.

evidence.quote: rather than a substitute for the automated loop.
evidence.support_explanation: Human-in-the-loop review is retained as a safeguard (continuation: "remains a complementary safeguard for this residual long tail").

evidence.quote: the skill excludes scripts/ and relies exclusively on pre-defined, verified system tools.
evidence.support_explanation: Skill action space is restricted to text and verified tools, simplifying diagnosis.

evidence.quote: Low consistency indicates a failure, triggering the bad-case analysis pipeline.
evidence.support_explanation: Judge verdict is both the evaluation metric and the trigger for evolution.

evidence.quote: Evaluated on five real-world cloud support scenarios spanning 1,883 tickets and 3,737 tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Dataset size; held-out set is the last 25% of each scenario.

evidence.quote: have medium risk due to external dependencies on tool availability.
evidence.support_explanation: Plans can recommend new tools whose availability must be verified; no gate applies this check in the loop.

evidence.quote: Cumulative gains increase at every iteration from each starting point
evidence.support_explanation: Monotone per-round gains reported on held-out set.

evidence.quote: It operates independently from the Failure Analyzer: the Judge determines whether a response is acceptable, while the Analyzer diagnoses why failures occur.
evidence.support_explanation: Judge and Analyzer are separate components.

evidence.quote: Synthesis enforces that every procedure traces to a mined resolution path
evidence.support_explanation: Creator grounds skills in mined historical resolution paths.

evidence.quote: Due to enterprise data privacy requirements, we use an internal LLM (Qwen3-Max) to process proprietary domain data.
evidence.support_explanation: Creator runs on an internal LLM; the evaluation split vs mining data overlap is not stated.

signatures.object: SKILL.md + references/ (incl. tools.json) of a deployed domain skill, edited only through a virtual file system (no scripts).
signatures.information: Per-bad-case analysis against the historical expert reply (divergence summary, four-dimension severities), aggregated category statistics and top-k representative cases, the current SKILL.md; internal knowledge-base search for the optimizer.
signatures.operation: Failure Analyzer (4 parallel LLM dimensions + deterministic verdict rules) -> category aggregation -> ReAct Diagnostician maps issues to SKILL.md locations and defect types (missing/insufficient/incorrect) and writes a prioritized plan -> Optimizer applies targeted additive edits with knowledge search and layered placement (SKILL.md / FAQ / link).
signatures.conditions: Minimal modification, do no harm (additive), evidence-based; offload to reference files beyond 500 lines/10K characters.
signatures.feedback: LLM-judge consistency verdict against expert reply identifies bad cases; failure records from the Analyzer.
signatures.selection_rule: None reported: every produced Skill_v(n+1) is committed; there is no candidate comparison, accept/reject, or rollback.
signatures.selection_data: Development splits 1-3 supply bad cases per round; held-out split 4 is evaluation only.
signatures.persistence: Versioned skill states v0-v3; later rounds start from the previous version.
signatures.later_use: The agent loads the skill as a meta-tool into context at inference time; the next round re-identifies bad cases with the current version.
signatures.claimed_effect: Held-out strict CR gains after v3: +10.99 (S_manual), +9.23 (S_domain), +11.60 (S_generic); +13.76pp over production legacy system.
signatures.failure_boundary: Knowledge failures plateau after v1; long-tail knowledge errors need humans; tool recommendations may require tools that do not exist.

signatures.object: Initial skill Skill_v0 synthesized from mined historical tickets and domain documentation (human-derived experience, not the agent own trajectories).
signatures.information: Historical ticket dialogues, operation logs, internal knowledge base; enterprise data privacy forces an internal LLM.
signatures.operation: Workflow mining -> tool mining by frequency -> knowledge extraction -> template-based synthesis with conditional branching and traceability constraints.
signatures.conditions: Fixed template; every procedure must trace to a mined resolution path.
signatures.selection_data: Historical tickets (overlap with the held-out evaluation tickets is not stated).
signatures.later_use: Start point for evolution and for RQ1 comparison.
signatures.claimed_effect: S_domain vs S_generic: +4.3pp strict and +3.6pp lenient on average.
signatures.failure_boundary: S_generic is denied domain data and built by a different creator model, so the comparison mixes information and model.

gap.author_gap: Generic skill creators lack domain grounding; once deployed there is no mechanism to trace execution failures back to skill deficiencies and drive targeted refinement.
gap.checked_gap: Both limitations are plausible for an enterprise skill setting, but the first gap is tested against a baseline deliberately denied domain data, so the result mainly shows that domain information helps. For the second gap the paper cites prompt-level optimizers (APE, OPRO, TextGrad), Reflexion/ExpeL and skill-evolution systems (MemSkill, EvoSkills, Steve-Evolving, AutoAgent) and asserts a structural difference (skill artifact, three-stage pipeline) without running any of them.
gap.lineage: Prompt optimizers (APE/OPRO/TextGrad) -> experience extraction (Reflexion/ExpeL) -> skill packages (Anthropic skills, SkillsBench) and skill-evolution systems -> diagnosis-then-patch pipeline specialized to ticketed support with historical expert replies as reference.
closest_adjacent: TextGrad / OPRO style text-gradient rewriting (cited, not compared)
EvoSkills, MemSkill, Steve-Evolving, AutoAgent skill evolution (cited, not compared)
Agent-in-the-Loop customer-support flywheel with human annotation (cited)
gap.residue: Structured failure-to-skill-section attribution in a domain with an abundant reference-reply signal.
gap.stakes: Skill quality in production support (held-out consistency +9 to +12 points over three rounds).
gap.method_response: Four-dimension failure analysis -> aggregated diagnosis with locations -> additive optimizer edits, repeated for three rounds.
gap.remaining_gap: No component ablation or optimizer baseline; no edit gate or rollback; absolute scores for the expert baseline are missing; single provider domain; judge-metric closed loop.
unresolved: Whether the multi-dimension Analyzer or the Diagnostician is needed relative to a direct rewrite from raw bad cases.
Whether evolved automatic skills beat the expert skill in absolute terms.

matches.reason: The pipeline splits skill improvement into analysis, aggregation, diagnosis and editing stages with structured artifacts handed between LLM agents and deterministic code. This is a decomposition-and-delegation structure; the artifacts are advisory plus judge-verified rather than solver-verified, hence partial.

rs_pattern.reason: Closest original operation is decompose-and-delegate with structured intermediate artifacts; C25 selected because the tactic allows closing the loop through the model own verify-and-revise path.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial - held-out gains show the pipeline can raise the judge metric, but no ablation shows the decomposition (as opposed to any rewriting from bad cases) is the cause.

matches.reason: Failures are attributed to specific SKILL.md locations with defect types and fixed through bounded additive edits. The re-run-and-retain-only-if-better step of H11 is missing: edits are committed without comparison.

Skill_v0 is compiled from mined historical resolution traces and documents into a structured package, but the source is human ticket history rather than agent interaction streams and there is no quality gate before use.

unassigned: Reference-reply-based divergence analysis (using the expert reply as the diagnostic reference) is not specifically covered by H11.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: split the task into sub-problems with typed handoff artifacts. Domain: attribute failures to specific skill sections then patch with bounded edits. The correspondence is the staged analysis -> diagnosis -> plan -> patch chain with structured artifacts.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: RS C25 requires verifiable closure and cost accounting; domain H11 requires re-validation before replacing the incumbent. Neither closure is present here (no commit gate), and the paper reports no cost.

expectations.question: Is the cost of the added structure (calls, tokens, latency) reported?
expectations.reason: No cost, token, latency or runtime figure appears anywhere in the text or appendices.

expectations.question: Does generalization extend beyond a single narrow benchmark or domain?

expectations.applies_when: Novelty relative to concurrent methods is claimed.

expectations.reason: No direct-rewrite, TextGrad/OPRO/Reflexion-style or skill-evolution baselines are run despite being cited.

expectations.reason: Appendix F gives failure-category distributions for one skill (108 bad cases) and the plateau analysis shows which failure types respond, but no experiment links stage choices to outcome.

expectations.question: Does the retention rule protect earlier wins (regression guard, rollback)?
expectations.reason: Only additive-edit instructions and versioned commits; no re-validation, accept/reject or rollback before the new version replaces the old.

expectations.applies_when: Failures are attributed to a decomposable artifact.

expectations.reason: Diagnostician maps issues to specific SKILL.md locations and defect types; edits are placed by type (knowledge sections, workflow steps, response templates).

expectations.applies_when: Many tasks fail for related reasons.
expectations.question: Are mechanisms diagnosed across tasks (clustered) before an edit?
expectations.reason: Per-case records are aggregated by category with frequencies and representative cases before diagnosis.

expectations.applies_when: The loop builds its own validation.
expectations.question: Is the certifying signal independent of the proposer (not self-constructed)?
expectations.reason: Reference replies are real expert answers, but the judge is an LLM whose model is not named (all experiments use Qwen3-Max, so it likely shares the backbone - our inference) and it both triggers evolution and scores the held-out set.

claims.text: Domain-contextualized creation yields better initial skills than a generic creator.
claims.setting: S_domain vs S_generic across five scenarios (split not stated).
claims.baseline_control: Claude Code (Sonnet-4.5) + mined tool schemas, no domain knowledge/tickets.
claims.result_denominator: Average +4.3pp strict, +3.6pp lenient; range +2.4 to +7.2pp strict per scenario.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A skill built with ticket/KB content outscored one built without it; model and information differences are confounded.

claims.text: The self-evolution loop progressively improves skill quality from three starting points on held-out data.
claims.setting: 3 rounds on chronological dev splits, evaluated on last 25% of tickets, 3 repeats.
claims.selection_vs_test: Held-out split never used in evolution; bad cases from dev splits only.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Supported as retained improvement on later held-out tickets within this domain; component contributions and uncertainty are unreported.

claims.text: Automated evolution can surpass manually curated expert knowledge.
claims.setting: Table 3 S_manual track; comparison with production legacy system.
claims.result_denominator: No absolute scores for S_manual or evolved variants.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Supported only in the narrow sense that the expert skill itself gained under evolution; comparison with legacy system is unmatched.

claims.result_denominator: Tool/style/clarification failures decline 13-21%; knowledge 0% in v2.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Authors report a ceiling for text-only skill optimization.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Three rounds of failure-analysis-driven skill rewriting on earlier chronological tickets raised LLM-judged consistency on a later held-out ticket split from three different starting skills (strict +9 to +12 points, mean of 3 runs), within one provider cloud-support domain.
not_supported: That evolved automatic skills outperform the expert skill (absolute scores missing).
That the Analyzer/Diagnostician/Optimizer decomposition is necessary (no ablation).
The +13.76pp gain over the legacy production system as a like-for-like result.
unresolved: Judge model, validation sample size, tickets used for creator mining, absolute scores, cost.
assessment.reproduction_note: Author-reported only; not reproduced. Not improver-level: the improvement mechanism itself is not changed or evaluated.

G.reason: Real, domain-specific limitations are stated and nearest neighbors are named, but the first gap is tested against a baseline denied domain data and the second against no competing optimizer, so the residual versus TextGrad/OPRO/skill-evolution neighbors is asserted structurally rather than shown.

M.reason: Well-reasoned chain: failure dimensions with deterministic aggregation, defect-type attribution to skill locations, additive optimizer with layered knowledge placement, and an analysis explaining the knowledge plateau. Not 4 because no distinguishing test against a direct bad-case-to-rewrite alternative is provided.

X.reason: Stages, schemas, thresholds (500 lines/10K characters), VFS and versioning are described and appendices are detailed, but the key retention conditions are absent: no acceptance gate, rollback, regression test on already-fixed cases, handling of recommended tools that do not exist, or staleness; prompts are not fully disclosed.

E.measurement.reason: Consistency Rate vs a single historical expert reply is judged by an LLM; judge validated at >90% on an unspecified subset, judge model not named, and the same judge triggers evolution, creating a metric-optimization loop. Absolute scores for the expert baseline and evolved variants are not reported.

E.causality.reason: Evolution from three starting points on a held-out split gives reasonable evidence that the loop causes gains over each v0, and the RQ1 contrast isolates domain information; but the creator contrast mixes model and information, no stage ablation or alternative optimizer is run, and the production-system comparison is unmatched.

E.holdout.reason: Chronological 25% held-out split never seen during evolution, evolution rounds fed with earlier splits only. Limits: single provider domain, one backbone, creator-mining data overlap with the held-out tickets unstated, no contamination check, no out-of-domain test.

E.statistics.reason: Large task counts (3,737 tasks) and 3 repeats, but only means are reported: no standard deviations, intervals or tests; per-scenario evolution results are not shown; no failure/regression counts of edits.

E.cost.reason: No token, call, latency, dollar or runtime figure is given for creation, evolution rounds or inference with loaded skills.
search_scope: Full text and Appendices A-F searched for cost, token, latency, GPU, budget, overhead, hours: zero occurrences
